intro: Split PDF breaks one document into several smaller files. Use it to share out a case file that was scanned in one go, send each chapter on its own or cut down a PDF that is too heavy for a web form. It runs in your browser without uploading the file, and pages are copied as they are: nothing is recompressed, so quality stays the same.

There are seven ways to cut. “Every N pages” makes equal parts; “Even and odd” gives two PDFs, one with the odd pages and one with the even ones; “In two halves” cuts the document down the middle. With “Custom” you type the pages after which to cut, such as “3, 7, 12”, and you get parts 1-3, 4-7, 8-12 and 13 to the end.

The other modes look at the content. “By top-level bookmarks” starts a new file at each chapter in the PDF's outline. “By maximum size” keeps adding pages to a part as long as it stays under the megabytes you set. “By blank pages” uses empty pages as separators and drops them.

Under “More options” you choose the name pattern for each part: {nombre} is the original file name, {n} the part number, and {desde} and {hasta} its first and last page. When there are several parts you can download them one by one or all together in a ZIP.

faq.q: What counts as a blank page?
faq.a: A page whose content draws nothing at all: no text, no images, no lines. A scanned blank sheet is an image, so it is not detected as empty; use the custom mode for those.

faq.q: What if a single page is bigger than the maximum size?
faq.a: That page goes into a file of its own even though it is over the limit, and the result tells you. To make it lighter, run it through Compress PDF first.

faq.q: Can I split several PDFs at once?
faq.a: Yes. Every file is split with the same options and all the parts can be downloaded together in a ZIP.

faq.q: What if the PDF has no bookmarks?
faq.a: The bookmark mode tells you the document has no top-level bookmarks and produces nothing. Add them with Edit PDF bookmarks or pick another mode.
